name: Image
s: The Image module provides a class with the same name which is used to represent a PIL image.
e: Create or transform raster images. Open, crop, resize, and generate thumbnails with bounded dimensions and aspect ratio rounding. Cropping returns a new raster; thumbnail changes its image object in place.

name: ImageChops
s: The ImageChops module contains a number of arithmetical image operations, called channel operations (“chops”).
e: Compare or combine pixel channels with difference, blend, composite and arithmetic. Most operations take one or two images and return a new image. Most are limited to 8-bit data with clipped results.

name: ImageCms
s: The ImageCms module provides color profile management support using the LittleCMS2 color management engine, based on Kevin Cazabon's PyCMS library.
e: Manage color profiles with LittleCMS2. Build or apply ICC transforms between profiles and image modes, choose rendering intent or soft proof. Requires compatible profiles and modes; pixel color conversion has no display layout contract.

name: ImageColor
s: The ImageColor module contains color tables and converters from CSS3-style color specifiers to RGB tuples.
e: Parse CSS-style color names, hexadecimal RGB or RGBA, and numeric color forms. getrgb returns channel values including alpha when encoded. getcolor converts for an image mode. Unsupported color syntax raises ValueError.

name: ImageDraw
s: The ImageDraw module provides simple 2D graphics for PIL.Image.Image objects.
e: Draw paths, text, and shapes onto a Pillow raster. Coordinates clip at image bounds. Default drawing replaces pixels; translucent blending depends on image and draw modes or a separate overlay.

name: ImageEnhance
s: The ImageEnhance module contains a number of classes that can be used for image enhancement.
e: Adjust color balance, brightness, contrast, or sharpness by a factor. The method returns an enhanced image and factor one gives an original copy. It changes pixel appearance within the same raster extent.

name: ImageFile
s: The ImageFile module provides support functions for the image open and save functions.
e: Feed bytes incrementally to a Pillow Parser and close to obtain the decoded image. Also exposes codec support and plugin classes. Data must form a supported image stream; decoding is distinct from editing output.

name: ImageFilter
s: The ImageFilter module contains definitions for a pre-defined set of filters, which can be used with the Image.filter() method.
e: Apply predefined or configurable raster filters including blur, sharpen, rank and lookup table filters. Image.filter consumes the filter and yields processed pixels. Kernel or mode choices constrain supported operations.

name: CSV Import
s: The following examples use the flights.csv file.
e: Read or write CSV in DuckDB. Configure header, delimiters, schema, null padding or error handling; CSV type options differ between read_csv and COPY. store_rejects skips faulty lines and records them.

name: CSV Auto Detection
s: When using read_csv, the system tries to automatically infer how to read the CSV file using the CSV sniffer.
e: Infer CSV dialect, column types, and header from a sample. Inspect a proposed configuration with sniff_csv or override options in read_csv. Compressed streams and stdin constrain sampling to the beginning.

name: Reading Faulty CSV Files
s: CSV files can come in all shapes and forms, with some presenting many errors that make the process of cleanly reading them inherently difficult.
e: Keep a CSV import running when rows are malformed. ignore_errors skips failures; store_rejects records bad lines and context in temporary tables. Projection and type choices can prevent an expected error from occurring.

name: CSV Import Tips
s: Below is a collection of tips to help when attempting to import complex CSV files.
e: Import tricky CSV by forcing a header, supplying names or types, or using COPY against an existing schema. union_by_name aligns multiple file schemas. These options operate in the reader, subject to file layout.

name: SELECT Clause
s: The SELECT clause specifies the list of columns that will be returned by the query.
e: Project the result columns and computed values. SELECT star EXCLUDE drops named columns from output; DISTINCT collapses returned duplicates. Projection occurs after FROM and filtering, and does not rewrite the source table.

name: FROM and JOIN Clauses
s: The FROM clause specifies the source of the data on which the remainder of the query should operate.
e: Choose query input and combine datasets with FROM, JOIN or a subquery. Supports table functions and joins with different unmatched-row behavior. Output projection and physical deletion belong to other statements.

name: WHERE Clause
s: The WHERE clause specifies any filters to apply to the data.
e: Filter query rows after choosing the FROM source. Conditions can select a subset by equality, LIKE or ILIKE. A SELECT WHERE predicate only controls result membership and does not delete stored rows.

name: GROUP BY Clause
s: The GROUP BY clause specifies which grouping columns should be used to perform any aggregations in the SELECT clause.
e: Combine rows by shared column values and compute aggregates. GROUP BY ALL derives grouping keys from nonaggregate SELECT columns. It changes result granularity and cannot retain a one-row-per-source-row view in general.

name: CSS Images Module Level 3
s: This module contains the features of CSS level 3 relating to the <image> type and some replaced elements.
e: Fit replaced image content to a browser box. object-fit contain preserves aspect ratio inside the box; cover fills and clips overflow. Layout size, visible sampling and source raster bytes remain separate.

name: CSS Display Module Level 3
s: This module describes how the CSS formatting box tree is generated from the document element tree and defines the display property that controls it.
e: Control how document elements generate rendered boxes. visibility hidden suppresses rendering while retaining layout; display none suppresses box generation. Descendants may override inherited visibility. The rules concern browser presentation rather than deleting source data.

name: Metadata Vocabulary for Tabular Data
s: Validation, conversion, display, and search of tabular data on the web requires additional metadata that describes how the data should be interpreted.
e: Annotate published tables with columns, datatypes, dialect and conversion metadata. suppressOutput can omit a column from generated output. Source values and columns still exist, and a conversion consumer must apply the annotation.

name: MapLibre Style Spec v8
s: Style specification version number.
e: Set map layer source, filter and visibility. A filter draws only features matching its expression; layout visibility can hide a layer. Features stay in the source, and zoom expressions in filters use integer zoom.
